account:
Today I have heard repeated but vague talk about a bridge or port change, usually associated with the bakery. Reports named the baker, innkeeper, freight, and neighbour as having been there; one report said the baker carried a sack of bread. These are things people told me, not changes I witnessed. The neighbour says they know no actual crossing change and have discouraged repeating the rumours as fact. The secretary likewise has no concrete information, although someone repeated a similar claim about town hall. I do not know whether these reports describe a real plan, ordinary conversations, or gossip, and I cannot establish their purpose. Asking the baker directly would be more useful than treating repetition as confirmation.

The mill stall had 74 hay bales when I inspected it, so I saw no evident grain shortage. My scheduled council correspondence did not materialise: the secretary reported no letters received and found only schedule books in the appointment chest. That is an absence of correspondence, not proof of anything hidden.

There is a definite town activity this evening: the approved 18:00 great hall lighting inspection with the builder and secretary, covering eight lanterns and the four tables. The neighbour says the builder told them the lighting is ready. That appears to be ordinary planned town maintenance. I have just had tea with the neighbour at the dockside cottage and said I must return for my 16:30 office appointment. It is now 16:02, so I need to leave promptly. I still have a feeling of being out of the loop, but nothing I have learned establishes a secret undertaking or its aim.
